decision.justification: Confirms the recommended order by matching the two existing reference behaviours rather than inventing one: store.default_db_path() (store.py:123) treats the env var as an override of the default, and default_layer() (api.py:1338) already implements explicit-argument > env > default. The bug was that DataLayer dropped the env layer, not that the order was wrong. DEFAULT_DB_PATH is now imported from store.py so the literal default has exactly one definition.
decision.single_resolution_function: api.resolve_store(explicit) -> (Path, source); DataLayer.__init__ (api.py) and default_layer() both call it. resolve_store_path() is the path-only form; resolve_journal_dir() applies the identical rule to RESEXTRACT_JOURNAL_DIR (same class of bug, same fix). app.py and __main__.py were not changed to call it directly: create_app passes store_path through to DataLayer, the one boundary.
decision.how: DataLayer.store_path / .store_source / .journal_dir / .journal_source attributes plus DataLayer.resolution() -> {store_path, store_source, journal_dir, journal_source} (api.py, 'Store resolution -- the ONE boundary' block); create_app also publishes store_path, store_source and store_resolution into app.state.dashboard (app.py) so the app and tests can read which store is live instead of inferring it. Precedence is documented in the same code block (previously: nowhere).

residual: A caller can still get the store wrong in three ways: (1) set RESEXTRACT_STATE_DB and then pass --store elsewhere - explicit wins by design, but the two must not be set inconsistently in one run; (2) pass a RELATIVE explicit path - only the default is cwd-relative, explicit paths are used verbatim, so a daemon whose cwd differs will resolve differently; (3) hold a DataLayer object across a change of RESEXTRACT_STATE_DB - default_layer() now rebuilds when the resolved paths change, but a layer a caller already holds is not invalidated. Also: tests/test_dashboard_auth.py still builds create_app() with no store_path and no env, so it opens the REAL state/state.sqlite (proven above by the recreated sidecars); it is now isolatable via RESEXTRACT_STATE_DB but that file is outside this unit's write paths.
